introduction: Job speaks for everyone who has known sleepless nights and days without hope. The psalm answers that the Lord "heals the broken in heart, and binds up their wounds." In the Gospel, Jesus takes Simon's mother-in-law by the hand and raises her up, and the whole town gathers at the door with its sick. Before dawn he slips away to pray, then moves on to preach in other towns. This week the Church keeps the World Day of the Sick. Let us bring all who suffer to Jesus.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, Jesus came to heal the sick and to proclaim the Good News. Let us bring to him the needs of the world.
intentions: For the Church: that, like Paul, she may proclaim the Good News freely and become all things to all people for the sake of the Gospel. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the sick, on this week of the World Day of the Sick: that they may feel the hand of Jesus raising them up, and find strength and peace. Let us pray to the Lord.
For doctors, nurses, caregivers, and chaplains: that they may serve the sick with skill, patience, and compassion. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who, like Job, are worn down by sleepless nights and long struggles: that the Lord may heal their broken hearts. Let us pray to the Lord.
For our parish: that we may begin each day with prayer, as Jesus did, and go out from it to serve others. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, you heal the broken in heart and bind up their wounds. Hear the prayers we bring you, and make us instruments of your healing love. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Raised by the hand
reflection.body:
Job does not soften his complaint: "I am made to possess months of misery, wearisome nights are appointed to me." Anyone who has kept watch beside a sick bed, or lain awake with worry, knows those nights. "Oh remember that my life is a breath," he says. Scripture lets us pray like this. Honest sorrow brought to God is still prayer.

The Gospel is a single day in Capernaum. Simon's mother-in-law lies sick with a fever. Jesus "came and took her by the hand and raised her up." She is healed, and she serves them. Being raised up by Jesus leads to service.

By evening the whole town is at the door. "All the city was gathered together at the door," and Jesus heals many. Then, "Early in the morning, while it was still dark, he rose up and went out, and departed into a deserted place, and prayed there." Even at the height of his success, Jesus makes time to be alone with his Father. When the disciples find him and say, "Everyone is looking for you," he does not go back to the crowd. He moves on to the next towns, because that is what he came for.

Paul shares the same urgency: "woe is to me if I don't preach the Good News." To win others, he says, "I have become all things to all men, that I may by all means save some."

This Thursday, 11 February, is the World Day of the Sick. Visit, call, or write to someone who is ill. Take their hand, as Jesus did. And find your own deserted place this week, even for ten minutes before dawn, to pray as he prayed.
